paper.title_en: A Quantum Algorithm for Computing All Eigenvalues and Eigenstates of Sparse Hermitian Matrices
paper.abstract_en: Computation of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a sparse Hermitian matrix is a fundamental problem in algebra, arising both as a problem of independent interest and as a key subroutine in a wide range of computational and scientific applications. In this work, we develop a quantum algorithm that determines the spectrum of a sparse Hermitian matrix, defined as the set of its distinct eigenvalues, and for each eigenvalue, prepares a corresponding eigenvector as a quantum state in its eigenspace. The eigenvalues are represented as binary strings with a prescribed precision, while the corresponding eigenvectors are kept as quantum states, eliminating the need to reconstruct their classical counterparts. The algorithm instead enables estimation of expectation values $\braket{x|M|x}$, where $|x⟩$ is a prepared eigenstate and $M$ is an observable. For an $n × n$ $s$-sparse Hermitian matrix $H$, dense methods based on Householder tridiagonalization and QR iteration compute all eigenvalues and eigenvectors in $𝒪(n^3)$ time. Exploiting sparsity, the Lanczos method computes all eigenvalues in $𝒪(n^2 s)$ time in exact arithmetic, but recovering all eigenvectors still requires $𝒪(n^3)$ time. In contrast, our algorithm runs in time $𝒪̃(n s^2 log^2 n / Δ_{min})$, where $Δ_{min}$ denotes the minimum spectral gap of the normalized matrix. For inverse gaps up to $Δ_{min}^{-1} = 𝒪(n)$, the most favorable scaling for $n$ distinct eigenvalues, attained by nearly uniformly spaced spectra such as those of perfect-state-transfer spin chains and the Sylvester-Kac matrix, and for sparsity up to $s = o(√(n)/log n)$, the proposed algorithm achieves an improved asymptotic runtime over the classical $𝒪(n^3)$ approach for computing all eigenvalues and eigenvectors, under standard sparse-access assumptions.
